overview: Black plays 2...c6 instead of defending e5 with a developing move, planning ...d5. White can take on e5 or play 3.d4 d5 4.Nc3, and Black is a pawn down or has an inferior version of a Caro-Kann/Scotch structure. It is an obscure line and I am not sure of details; strong players choose the normal 2...Nc6.

white_ideas.idea: Take the e5 pawn with Nxe5 and keep the extra pawn.
Or play d4 and Nc3, building a bigger centre.

black_ideas.idea: Strike with ...d5 to gain time and open lines.
Develop with ...Bd6 or ...Nf6 for the pawn.

typical_structures.structure: Black's ...c6/...d5 centre against White's extra e-pawn or a d4/e4 centre.

character.notes: Black is playing for a pawn with unclear compensation; I cannot say how sharp it gets.

gambit.notes: White can simply take e5 with Nxe5 and keep the pawn.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider it unsound; Black gets little for the pawn.

structure.notes: After Nxe5 d5 the centre is open or semi-open; I am unsure.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever choose it.

level.notes: Dubious; not a good first choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.d4 d5
sublines_that_differ.how: White declines the pawn and plays for a space edge.

character.reason: Unclear; it is not known for forcing play, just a pawn deficit.

gambit.reason: Black allows Nxe5 for ...d5 and development.

soundness.reason: Black gets little for the pawn.

structure.reason: Unclear; the centre may open after ...d5.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever play it.

plans.reason: No clear plan from the evidence.
